column2: What is the policy for sick leave?
column3:
The policy for sick leave in the Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement is as follows:

* Sick leave benefits are not cumulative and are not cashable upon termination of employment or at any other time (5.45.06).
* Sick leave benefits for any period of absence following notice of termination of employment will not be payable without substantiating medical evidence (5.45.05).
* Sick leave benefits defined in this Article may not be granted under the following circumstances:
 + Intentionally self-inflicted injuries or diseases (5.45.11(a)).
 + Pregnancy (however, complications due to pregnancy are covered by sick leave provisions, upon submission of a medical certificate) (5.45.11(b)).
 + While vacation pay is also being received (5.45.11(c)).
 + Wilful participation in riots, wars or violent or uncontrolled demonstrations or protests (5.45.11(d)).
 + Injuries or diseases sustained while committing a criminal act for which the Member has been found to be guilty by a duly constituted court or while serving a prison sentence (5.45.11(e)).
* To have a sick leave benefits period reinstated up to the maximum, Members who have been absent and in receipt of sick leave benefits must return to full duties for at least one (1) full working day in the case of a completely unrelated and different disability cause, and for thirty (30) calendar days in the case of the same disability cause (5.45.04).
* Sick leave benefits will be reduced by the amount of any Worker's Compensation benefits or similar disability income benefits which the Member is eligible to receive by reason of accident or sickness, from a government plan, except Employment Insurance (5.45.07).

It is also worth noting that the agreement requires a report to be submitted for any sick leave period in excess of five (5) consecutive working days, and that the report shall not contain any diagnosis of the Member's condition, unless the Member, in consultation with the Union, requests that the diagnosis be included (7.55.7).

column2: Can a faculty member be forced to move to a different campus?
column3:
According to the text, a faculty member can be forced to move to a different campus, but only if the conditions specified in their initial nomination letter are met. (Article 8.55.2)

However, it's worth noting that members who apply for a course outside their normal campus or apply specifically for a position at a specific campus will not be reimbursed for travel. (Article 12.10)

It's also mentioned that employees hired for a period of 12 months or less are not normally eligible for reimbursement of their relocation expenses, unless the Vice-President, Academic and Provost grants special permission. (Article 8.55.3)

In any case, if a faculty member is forced to move to a different campus, they would be required to pay the associated relocation expenses.

column2: How is teaching load calculated?
column3:
According to the Collective Agreement 2008-11 and 2011-14, teaching load is calculated as follows:

For Teaching Members:

* The maximum normal teaching load per academic year is 2 full courses or 12 credit equivalents in the Faculty of Science and Engineering, and 2.5 full courses or 15 credit equivalents in other Faculties.
* For Sessional Members, the workload is determined by the Chair/Coordinator and recommended to the President, with a maximum of 15 credits in the fall/winter session and 9 credits in the spring session.

For Professional Librarian and Archivist Members, the normal hours of scheduled student contact shall not exceed 12 per week, scheduled fairly and equitably, and on the recommendation of the Department.

The calculation of teaching load can also take into account past practices, but only if these practices have not been the result of members undertaking voluntarily unpaid overloads due to budgetary pressures or unless specific provisions in the contract state otherwise.

column2: What is the policy on academic freedom?
column3:
According to the Collective Agreement 2018-2021, Academic freedom is the right to search for truth, knowledge, and understanding and to express freely what one believes. The University as an institution and the community of its scholars have a duty to protect and defend the search for knowledge and truth by all that inquire, teach, offer professional services, and learn under its auspices.

The policy on academic freedom includes:

* The right to freedom in teaching, research, and scholarship
* The right to express one's opinions about the University, its administration, and the system in which one works
* The right to participate in professional and representative academic bodies
* The right to engage in service to the institution and the community
* The right to contribute to social change through free expression on matters of public interest

It is also important to note that academic freedom does not confer legal immunity and requires the acknowledgement of the work of others and the acceptance of responsibility for one's own beliefs and utterances.

column2: Quelles sont les étapes formelles de la procédure de grief ?
column3:
Selon l'article 12.10.10 de la Convention collective 2008-11, les étapes formelles de la procédure de grief sont les suivantes :

1. Le plaignant dépose un avis par écrit auprès du Vice-recteur aux études et Provost, ou auprès du président du Syndicat, dans les trente (30) jours ouvrables suivant la date à laquelle le demandeur a été informé du fait ou de la décision causant le grief.
2. Au plus tard vingt (20) jours après la réception de l’avis de grief formel, le représentant de l’Employeur rencontre le représentant du Syndicat pour tenter de régler le grief.
3. Si le grief est réglé à cette étape, le règlement est dressé et contresigné par le représentant du Syndicat et le représentant de l’Employeur au plus tard quinze (15) jours ouvrables après la réunion où le règlement est atteint.
4. Si le grief n'est pas réglé à cette étape, le représentant de la partie répondant au grief transmet par écrit au représentant de l'autre partie les raisons du rejet du grief.

Il est important de noter que si le représentant du Syndicat et le représentant de l’Employeur ne peuvent pas régler le grief dans les quinze (15) jours ouvrables qui suivent la ou les réunions indiquées à l’Article 12.10.11 (c) ci-dessus, le processus d'arbitrage est initié selon les dispositions de l'Article 12.15.

	+ transport, emballage, mise en caisse, déballage des articles du ménage et des effets personnels

Il convient de noter que les frais de déménagement remboursés constituent un prêt dont le nouveau membre fait grâce à l'employeur après avoir complété trois ans de service continu à l'Université, selon les dispositions de l'article 8.55.4 de la convention collective 2015-2018.

column2: Que faire en cas de contradiction entre la convention et une politique de l'université ?
column3:
En cas de contradiction entre la convention collective et une politique de l'université, il est important de suivre les étapes suivantes :

1. La première étape consiste à vérifier si la politique de l'université correspond à la convention collective. Si oui, la politique de l'université doit être suivie.
2. Si la politique de l'université ne correspond pas à la convention collective, il est recommandé de contacter le Département ou l'École pour obtenir des informations supplémentaires.
3. Si la contradiction persiste, il est possible de demander à l'Université de négocier une adaptation de la politique en question.
4. Si l'Université refuse de négocier, il est possible de demander à la Confédération des syndicats nationaux des professeurs d'enseignement supérieur du Québec (CSNQ) ou au syndicat du Membre en question de fournir un soutien et des conseils pour résoudre la contradiction.

Il est important de noter que les Parties ont accepté dans la convention collective que les modifications demandées par les organismes externes ne nécessitent pas d'approbation préalable, ce qui suggère que les politiques de l'Université doivent être compatibles avec la convention collective.

column2: Y a-t-il des dispositions pour le congé de maternité ?
column3: Oui, il y a des dispositions pour le congé de maternité dans la convention collective. L'article 7.60 prévoit des congés de maternité pour les membres à temps plein ou chargés de cours permanent qui sont enceintes, ainsi que des congés parentsaux et de adoption. Le congé de maternité peut être pris de 17 semaines, et les membres reçoivent des prestations complémentaires si elles ont complété au moins 12 mois de service ininterrompu. Les membres en congé parental sont également éligibles à un congé parental de 5 jours, ainsi qu'à des prestations complémentaires.

column2: What happens if a conflict arises between university policy and the collective agreement?
column3:
According to Article 10.01 of the Collective Agreement, members of the unit of negotiation are expected to adhere to the activities listed, which include:

(a) They will perform the tasks of teaching assigned to them in accordance with the present Collective Agreement.

(b) They will engage in research and pursue scholarly activities.

(c) They will provide their services to the University.

(d) They will provide their services to the profession and the community.

However, it does not explicitly state what happens if a conflict arises between university policy and the collective agreement.

It is worth noting that Article 10.01 does not provide a clear answer to this question, and it is likely that further interpretation and clarification would be needed in the event of a conflict between the two.

column2: What is the role of an arbitrator?
column3:
According to the Collective Agreement, the role of an arbitrator is to:

* Have the authority to issue interim orders requiring the Employer to provide relief (Article 36.02)
* Not have the power to alter, add to, or modify the Agreement in any respect (Article 36.02)
* Not make any decisions inconsistent with the provisions of the Collective Agreement (Article 24.03)
* Not alter, modify, add to, or amend any part of the Collective Agreement (Article 24.03)
* Make a decision that is final and binding upon the Parties, including the Employee or Employees concerned, in the absence of a majority decision (Article 11.15.5)

Additionally, the arbitrator's decision must be based on the standards set out in Article 5.50 - Assessment of a Member's Performance, which includes:

* A record of satisfactory teaching in the pre-tenure years
* A record of satisfactory scholarly activity
* A record of contributions to University governance and administrative duties
* The applicant's meeting of formal educational or professional qualifications for the rank of Assistant Professor and bilingualism qualifications

The arbitrator's decision must also be flexible and take into account the nature and scope of the applicant's past teaching activities, as well as any evidence of recognized problems and improvements made by the applicant.

Il s'agit d'une organisation professionnelle qui représente les professeurs de l'Université Laurentienne, et non un Syndicat.

column2: Y a-t-il un congé prévu pour une assignation à témoigner au tribunal ?
column3:
Oui, il y a un congé prévu pour une assignation à témoigner au tribunal, mais il ne s'agit pas d'un congé payé. Selon l'article 7.45.1, un congé payé est normalement accordé aux Membres, sauf s'ils sont bénéficiaires d'un congé non rémunéré, s'ils sont cités en justice en tant que juré, témoin ou expert-conseil, ou cités à comparaître devant un tribunal ou tout organe judiciaire ou statutaire du Canada habilité à contraindre les témoins à comparaître devant lui.

Par contre, il n'y a pas de congé spécifiquement prévu pour une assignation à témoigner au tribunal, mais les dispositions de l'article 7.45 s'appliquent dans ce cas, et le Membre doit signaler par écrit son absence imminente et apporter une preuve de sa comparution effective si on le demande.
